clue.text: Special legislation to introduce noodles in religious service

indicators.note: the legislation is made to take the noodles into itself, so one word is opened up to hold the other

parts.note: an act is a piece of legislation passed by parliament
ramen are Japanese wheat noodles served in broth

explanation.surface: A new law is passed to bring noodles into a church ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' puts RAMEN inside ACT, giving ACRAMENT after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a rite of the Christian church such as baptism or the Eucharist.

clue.text: Largely biased about way of approaching evidence of arson?

indicators.note: about tells us the shortened word goes around the other piece
largely means most of the word is used, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: skew means slant or bias, as in a skewed view
MO stands for modus operandi, a person's method or way of going about things

explanation.surface: Someone prejudiced looks at a fire scene with a slanted eye for proof it was set deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' trims SKEW to SKE, and 'about' wraps that around MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Where there is fire there are fumes rising, the first sign that a building has been torched; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Nothing in the box, but possibly something on the box?

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the container word

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: An empty container is contrasted with what might be showing on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television, so something on it could be an animated show; the same phrase in the wordplay is a literal box.
explanation.definitionFit: An animated film is one kind of programme shown on television, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Performance overlooked in huge escapade

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the performance word is removed from the larger word

parts.note: gigantic means huge
a gig is a musical performance

explanation.surface: A show gets forgotten in the middle of some enormous adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' removes GIG from GIGANTIC, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or absurd caper, a piece of foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Group of nations not honest, in US view? That's sounding good

parts.note: EU is the European Union, a group of nations
phony means fake or insincere, and this is the American spelling of the British phoney

explanation.surface: A bloc of countries is judged dishonest by Americans, and someone approves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in US view' explains the spelling without the E that British English uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantness of sound, as in a harmonious combination of words, is the meaning of this noun.

clue.text: Article on treatment of angina taking a different line

indicators.note: on puts the article first in a down clue, sitting on top of the rest

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: treatment works the letters over, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about how a heart condition is treated, offering an alternative view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment of' rearranges ANGINA into NAGAIN; 'on' sets THE above it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to introduce a contrasting point, as 'on the other hand' does.

clue.text: Dance put off — piano unavailable

indicators.note: unavailable says the piano is not there, so its letter is removed

parts.note: repel means to put off or drive away
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A dance is cancelled because there is no piano to play for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unavailable' removes P from REPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Further test, subsequently overturned, involving group of scientists

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the reversed word holds the other piece
overturned in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: later means subsequently
RI is the Royal Institution, a British scientific body

explanation.surface: A further trial involving scientists is later overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses LATER to RETAL, and 'involving' puts RI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A second hearing of a case in court is a fresh examination of the evidence.

clue.text: Transport facility transformed by alien race

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Extraterrestrials remake a transport hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed by' rearranges ALIEN RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a waterway in New York State linking the Hudson River with the Great Lakes, built for shipping goods.

clue.text: Offended feelings, getting cross after rejecting bread

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the joined pieces are read backwards
after puts the cross word behind the feelings word

parts.note: pets are fits of pique, as in being in a pet
a rood is a cross, especially one in a church

explanation.surface: Someone sulks and becomes angry after their bread is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' reverses PETS + ROOD as a whole. A doorstep is British slang for a very thick slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickly cut slab of a loaf is called this in informal British usage.

clue.text: Necessitate declining Frenchman crazy about one

indicators.note: declining means refusing, so the Frenchman turns down his place and his letter goes
about tells us the crazy word goes around the numeral

parts.note: mental is informal for crazy
one is the Roman numeral I
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman refuses because of a mad passion for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside MENTAL to give MENTAIL, then 'declining' drops the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something unavoidable as a consequence, as when a job involves travel, is to require it.

clue.text: Brave, hot, sexy, timeless

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: timeless says without time, and T is the abbreviation for time

parts.note: erotic means sexy

explanation.surface: A list of qualities that might describe an ageless film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T (time) from EROTIC, leaving EROIC after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous and bold, like the deeds of a legendary champion.

clue.text: Ordinary expression when eating dessert is unvarying

parts.note: O is short for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the expression word holds the dessert

parts.note: a face is a facial expression, as in pulling a face
a pie can be served as a sweet course

explanation.surface: Someone's face looks the same while eating pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when eating' puts PIE inside FACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means of the same kind or consistent with the rest, so all alike.

clue.text: Gorgeous guy hosting party within an island

indicators.note: within puts the party inside the two-letter word

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A handsome man throws a party on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts DO inside AN; 'hosting' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a youth loved by Aphrodite for his beauty, so any very handsome young man.

clue.text: Uppity servant receiving nasty boils in devil-worship

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the reversed word holds the rearranged one
uppity in a down clue says the word goes up, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

indicators.note: nasty signals that the next word is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An arrogant servant gets horrible boils during satanic rites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppity' reverses MAID to DIAM; 'nasty' rearranges BOILS to BOLIS; 'receiving' puts that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of the devil, or sorcery invoking demons, is this practice.

clue.text: Princess brought in to initiate recreation area

indicators.note: brought in to means put inside, so the name goes inside the other word

parts.note: to spark something is to start or initiate it
Kate, the Princess of Wales, is a well-known royal

explanation.surface: A royal is invited to open a new public park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in to' places KATE inside SPARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A place with ramps and bowls built for skateboarders to ride is a leisure ground.

clue.text: Long seen around Long Island with grand new contender?

indicators.note: seen around says the first word is placed around the next piece

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
LI is the abbreviation for Long Island, New York
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone pines on Long Island for a fresh challenger, a thousand dollars at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' puts LI inside YEARN, and G follows. A young racehorse in its first year is a possible new runner, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse between one and two years old is about to start racing, so a fresh competitor.

clue.text: Force beginning to coerce a sailor to perform

indicators.note: beginning to says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: Someone uses pressure to make a seaman put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is a northern English word for a waterfall, which is what the answer also means; the surface reads it as compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: A large waterfall is both a force (in the north of England) and a cataract.

clue.text: Succeeded leading soldiers, infiltrating a network? I never succeeded

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so those pieces go into the network

parts.note: a LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: leading puts the succeeded letter in front of the soldiers

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A successful officer leads troops into a computer network, though the speaker failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' puts S + OR inside A LAN. The definition is a loser's own words: a horse or person who did not win.
explanation.definitionFit: Said by a runner who finished unplaced, a loser in a race or contest, in their own voice.

clue.text: Beachwear mostly failing one

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: tanking is slang for failing badly
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Most swimwear lets one down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' removes the last letter of TANKING, leaving TANKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit combining a tank top with bikini bottoms is worn at the seaside.

clue.text: Quill leaked needing trimming a bit

parts.note: the nib is the writing point of a quill pen

indicators.note: trimming means cutting the end off, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: bled means leaked, as colours or ink run

explanation.surface: A leaky quill pen needs its tip cut back slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing trimming' cuts D from BLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bite of food is a morsel, a little piece.

clue.text: Road blockage, largely conspicuous, left on a road

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, so the final letter goes

parts.note: bold means striking or conspicuous

explanation.surface: A highly visible obstruction stands on the left of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts BOLD to BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A short thick post set in the street stops vehicles passing, so it blocks traffic.

clue.text: Rocky neoliths in ancient German region

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the following word's letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Unsteady standing stones stand in an old German territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' rearranges NEOLITHS.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic duchy in northern Germany, now part of Schleswig-Holstein, also gave its name to a breed of cattle.

clue.text: A line in a remarkable opera

indicators.note: in puts the article and the line inside the other word

parts.note: some means remarkable, as in that was some party

explanation.surface: A single line in an outstanding opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A + L inside SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Richard Strauss's 1905 opera based on Oscar Wilde's play.

clue.text: AI output with electronic slant

parts.note: slop is a current term for low-quality content churned out by artificial intelligence
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Machine-generated text with a digital bias.
explanation.walkthrough: Slop is recent slang for careless AI-generated material.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline or gradient is a tilt in the ground.

clue.text: Detective increasingly seen around Society

indicators.note: seen around says the first word is placed around the next piece

parts.note: more and more means increasingly, so more alone serves

explanation.surface: An investigator is spotted more often in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' puts S inside MORE. Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse is a famous fictional police officer in Oxford.

clue.text: Current mistake, entering when reversing a Ford

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so those pieces go into the reversed word
reversing means the short word is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
I is the symbol for electric current
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A driver makes an electrical fault while backing a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns AS into SA, and 'entering' puts I + ERR inside it. The Sierra was a Ford family car sold in Britain in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Sierra was a popular model of the car maker in the 1980s.

clue.text: I tour US city and attempt admiration

parts.note: to do a place is informal for touring it, as in doing Europe
LA is Los Angeles
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone visits Los Angeles and tries to admire it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour' gives DO, as tourists 'do' a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of images or excessive adoration of a person is extreme devotion.

clue.text: A sign wicket will fall in maidens?

indicators.note: a fallen wicket goes, so its letter is removed

parts.note: maidens are young women
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket question: will a batsman be out during maiden overs?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored; here maidens are young women instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent of things to come is a prophetic token.

clue.text: Crucial point for one writing back about supply

indicators.note: about says the reversed pieces go around the supply word
back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
ink stands for writing, as in putting pen to paper
to feed is to supply

explanation.surface: An author stuck at a critical moment, writing back about provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses EG + INK to KNIGE, and 'about' puts FEED inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A precarious, finely balanced state where outcomes could go either way is a tipping point.
